newsitem.title: UK: Newcastle United shares make winning start.
newsitem.headline: Newcastle United shares make winning start.

text.p: English premier league soccer club Newcastle United made a successful debut on the London Stock Exchange on Wednesday when its shares traded at a premium to the offer price.
The shares stood at 141.5p by 0810 GMT, against an offer price of 135p in a flotation which gave the club an initial market capitalisation of 193 million stg.
"There were a lot of unknowns but obviously it's a success as far as today is concerned," said analyst Nick Batram of Greig, Middleton.
The retail part of the offer was limited to season ticket holders and members of staff. The club said demand was also significantly greater than supply for the institutional side of the offer.

The flotation raised 54 million stg gross, which will be used to repay borrowings, pay for future instalments of transfer fees for current players and fund proposed training and youth development facilities.

Shares in the expanding soccer sector have fallen heavily in recent weeks as the euphoria surrounding potential pay-per-view income subsided and the extra supply allowed investors to pick and choose their stocks more carefully.

Batram said that Newcastle were well placed to succeed as a business but noted that the north-east club could not yet be classed among English soccer's elite, along with current champions Manchester United, Liverpool and Arsenal.
"Newcastle have great ingredients with strong local support, a developing brand and a reputation for the kind of exciting soccer which attracts television audiences," he said.
"The next stage is to turn that into profits and for a lot of people the jury is still out -- they want to see the company deliver," he added.
Newcastle have spent 50 million stg on players over the past five years, recruiting stars such as England captain Alan Shearer.
The investment has turned Newcastle from an ailing first division team into one of the leading lights in the premier league, although they have yet to win a major trophy.

There was upheaval earlier this season when manager Kevin Keegan resigned. He has been replaced by Kenny Dalglish and the new man is expected to reshape the squad this summer through trading in the transfer market.
